purpose: Measure whether explicit possibility-family preprocessing can preserve strong family coverage while moving grouping work off the hot read path.
scope_guard: This does not establish universal database superiority. The SQLite group/window baseline is a strong conventional same-family-semantic counterbaseline. The precompiled-head result measures a materialized semantic-preprocessor pattern with build/update cost explicitly retained.
derived_observations: Flat top-k is the latency floor but structurally redundant when several bindings represent one explicit possibility family.
A conventional SQL window/group baseline fully repairs family coverage but performs grouping/ranking at query time in this fixture.
Precompiled family heads preserve the same family coverage while shifting grouping cost to compile/update time.

The current naive targeted maintenance still re-sorts all family heads, so its roughly 2x update advantage is not an asymptotic claim; a balanced/order-statistics or factorized maintained view is the stronger next mechanism.
Promotion remains gated by measured lifetime/amortization, real EAP provenance/negative-space semantics, target-runner execution, and downstream Frank task outcomes.
external_fusion: F-IVM: factorized computation plus hierarchical incremental views supports efficient analytics under updates.
GeoRAG / 2026 coverage work: plain top-k can over-cover one demand mode and miss other necessary modes; diversity/coverage must remain quality-bounded.
next_falsifiers: Run F1 and F2 against exact current EAP on self-hosted target runner.
If F2 accuracy wins but wrapper materialization cost is high, move explicit-family grouping natively between candidate_rank.sort() and max_items truncation.
Compare native factorized EAP against SQLite window/group baseline plus exact-key bypass, not against a weak FTS-only baseline.
Measure downstream model/tool-route success under fixed context budget, not retrieval metrics alone.
